caption_link.limitation: The source provides matching numeric IDs only. It does not provide an original post URL, date, media link, or an explicit asset-to-caption key.

inspection.evidence_scope: Source-bound start, material-intermediate, and near-complete frames were extracted from the original local GIF and visually inspected at full canvas size; metadata came from that same source file.

motion_sampling.method: Three source-bound frame samples extracted from the original local GIF for review; no derivative was added to the corpus.
motion_sampling.limitation: Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

visual_anatomy.title: A short case-study headline sits above two large lavender metric cards, with the central question deferred to a long rounded strap at the bottom.
visual_anatomy.layout: A centred time-series panel anchors the page; two spike callouts travel upward to large specimen frames, while the headline/metrics above and explanation strap below frame the evidence.
visual_anatomy.reading_order: Headline → two reported metric cards → time-series spikes and their callout lines → specimen frames → bottom explanation strap.
visual_anatomy.typography: Large light sans headline, heavy black metric text, compact axis/date labels, and rough display emphasis appearing in the animated explanation strap.
visual_anatomy.colour: Lavender is used for metric cards, specimen-frame masks, and outlines; the graph line is teal, allowing the evidence path to differ from the framing colour.
visual_anatomy.surface: White page, a thin dark-lavender panel outline, large masked specimen rectangles, sparse chart grid lines, circular spike targets, and soft shadows.
visual_anatomy.modules: Headline/metric pair, one time-series with two highlighted peaks, two evidence specimens, and one succinct explanatory prompt.
visual_anatomy.density: Medium: a single chart and two linked specimens keep the case-study argument focused rather than overloading it with metrics.

motion.observed_state_change: The opening sample keeps the two specimen frames masked in solid purple; the material-intermediate sample reveals two distinct creative specimens above their corresponding chart peaks and begins writing a method phrase in the lower strap; the near-complete sample is partway through the loop/reset.
motion.motion_job: Reveal the proposed evidence behind outcome peaks so the viewer sees a claim, a time-series event, and the underlying artefact as a connected argument.
motion.limitation: Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

transferable_mechanism.reader_job: Understand what observed output coincided with which concrete artefact instead of accepting a naked outcome statistic.
transferable_mechanism.argument_shape: Outcome timeline with linked evidence specimens.
transferable_mechanism.mechanism: Anchor the story in a dated measurement, mark the relevant events, then reveal the inspectable artefacts associated with those events through direct callouts.
transferable_mechanism.use_condition: Use only with permission-backed evidence, stable metric definitions, and a clear distinction between temporal association and demonstrated causation.

anti_copy_boundary: Do not reuse the source’s named case, figures, time series, specimen images, chart spikes, metric-card treatment, purple masks, lower strap wording, or reveal sequence.

claim_boundary.note: The visual makes named case-study and percentage-performance claims. The supplied corpus does not independently verify the metrics, the causal implication, the specimen provenance, or the caption association.
